questions.question: The human eye forms an image on the retina that is
questions.explanation: The eye lens is a converging lens. It forms a real, inverted image on the retina. The brain interprets this inverted image as upright.

questions.question: The part of the eye that controls the amount of light entering it is the
questions.explanation: The iris controls the size of the pupil, thereby regulating the amount of light entering the eye.

questions.question: The light-sensitive screen at the back of the eye is the
questions.explanation: The retina is the light-sensitive layer at the back of the eye where the image is formed.

questions.question: The ability of the eye to focus objects at different distances is called
questions.explanation: Accommodation is the ability of the eye to change the focal length of its lens to focus on objects at different distances.

questions.question: The eye defect in which a person cannot see distant objects clearly is called
questions.explanation: Short sight (myopia) is the defect where distant objects appear blurred because the image forms in front of the retina.

questions.question: Short sightedness is corrected using a
questions.explanation: Short sightedness is corrected using a concave (diverging) lens, which diverges light before it enters the eye.

questions.question: Long sightedness is corrected using a
questions.explanation: Long sightedness (hypermetropia) is corrected using a convex (converging) lens.

questions.question: Astigmatism is corrected using a
questions.explanation: Astigmatism is caused by uneven curvature of the cornea or lens. It is corrected using a cylindrical lens.

questions.question: Presbyopia, the loss of accommodation in old age, is corrected using
questions.explanation: Presbyopia involves difficulty in seeing both near and distant objects. It is corrected using bifocal lenses.

questions.question: The least distance of distinct vision for a normal human eye is about
questions.explanation: The least distance of distinct vision for a normal eye is about 25 cm.

questions.question: The range of accommodation of a normal human eye is
questions.explanation: A normal eye can focus from the near point (about 25 cm) to infinity. Therefore the range is 0.25 m to infinity.

questions.question: The camera part that corresponds to the retina of the eye is the
questions.explanation: The film in a camera is the light-sensitive surface where the image is formed, corresponding to the retina.

questions.question: The camera part that corresponds to the iris of the eye is the
questions.explanation: The diaphragm controls the amount of light entering the camera, corresponding to the iris.

questions.question: The part of the camera whose function is similar to that of the eyelid is the
questions.explanation: The shutter controls the time for which light enters the camera, similar to the eyelid.

questions.question: The distance between the lens and the film in a camera is adjusted in order to
options: Focus the image on the film
questions.explanation: Moving the lens changes the image distance so that a sharp image is focused on the film.

questions.question: A simple microscope consists of
options: One convex and one concave lens
questions.explanation: A simple microscope is just a single convex lens used as a magnifying glass.

questions.question: In normal use, a simple microscope produces an image that is
questions.explanation: When an object is placed within the focal length of a convex lens, the image is virtual, erect, and magnified.

questions.question: A compound microscope consists of
options: One convex and one concave lens
questions.explanation: A compound microscope uses two convex lenses: the objective and the eyepiece.

questions.question: In a compound microscope, the objective lens has
options: A longer focal length than the eyepiece
A shorter focal length than the eyepiece
The same focal length as the eyepiece
questions.explanation: The objective lens has a short focal length to produce high magnification.

questions.question: The image formed by the objective lens of a compound microscope is
questions.explanation: The objective lens forms a real, inverted, magnified image that acts as the object for the eyepiece.

questions.question: The final image in a compound microscope is
questions.explanation: The eyepiece acts as a magnifying glass on the intermediate image, producing a virtual, erect, magnified final image.

questions.question: An astronomical telescope consists of an objective lens of
options: Short focal length and an eyepiece of short focal length
Long focal length and an eyepiece of short focal length
Short focal length and an eyepiece of long focal length
Long focal length and an eyepiece of long focal length
questions.explanation: An astronomical telescope uses an objective of long focal length and an eyepiece of short focal length.

questions.question: The angular magnification of an astronomical telescope in normal adjustment is given by
questions.explanation: In normal adjustment, angular magnification M = fo / fe.

questions.question: An astronomical telescope is said to be in normal adjustment when the final image is at
questions.explanation: In normal adjustment, the final image is formed at infinity, so the eye is relaxed.

questions.question: In normal adjustment, the separation between the objective and eyepiece of an astronomical telescope is
questions.explanation: The separation between the lenses in normal adjustment is fo + fe.

questions.question: An astronomical telescope of objective focal length 100cm and eyepiece focal length 10cm is in normal adjustment. The separation of the lenses is
questions.explanation: Separation = fo + fe = 100 + 10 = 110 cm.

questions.question: The final image of an astronomical telescope in normal adjustment is
questions.explanation: The final image is virtual and inverted.

questions.question: A terrestrial telescope differs from an astronomical telescope because it has
options: An extra converging lens to erect the image
An extra diverging lens to erect the image
questions.explanation: A terrestrial telescope uses an extra converging lens (erecting lens) to make the final image erect.

questions.question: A Galilean telescope uses as its eyepiece a
questions.explanation: A Galilean telescope uses a concave lens as its eyepiece.

questions.question: A Galilean telescope produces a final image that is
questions.explanation: The Galilean telescope produces a virtual, erect image.

questions.question: A periscope uses
options: Two plane mirrors or totally reflecting prisms
questions.explanation: A periscope uses two plane mirrors or totally reflecting prisms to bend light.

questions.question: Totally reflecting prisms are preferred to mirrors in periscopes because
options: They do not give multiple images and reflect more light
questions.explanation: Totally reflecting prisms reflect more light and avoid multiple images.

questions.question: The instrument used to obtain different colour patterns by multiple reflection is the
questions.explanation: A kaleidoscope uses multiple reflections to produce colourful patterns.

questions.question: A film projector is used to project an image on a screen. The image formed is
questions.explanation: A projector forms a real, inverted, magnified image on the screen.

questions.question: For a projector to produce a magnified real image, the slide must be placed
options: At the principal focus of the lens
Between the principal focus and twice the focal length
questions.explanation: To get a magnified real image, the object must be between F and 2F.

questions.question: The image on a projector screen appears
options: Magnified and inverted relative to the slide
Magnified and erect relative to the slide
Diminished and inverted relative to the slide
questions.explanation: The screen image is magnified and inverted relative to the slide.

questions.question: A pinhole camera forms an image that is
questions.explanation: A pinhole camera forms a real, inverted image.

questions.question: Increasing the size of the hole of a pinhole camera makes the image
questions.explanation: A larger hole admits more light but makes the image blurred.

questions.question: An optical fibre transmits light by repeated
questions.explanation: Optical fibres transmit light by total internal reflection.

questions.question: Optical fibres are used in
questions.explanation: Optical fibres are used in communication and endoscopy.

questions.question: The principle that makes optical fibre work is
questions.explanation: Optical fibres work on the principle of total internal reflection.

questions.question: A magnifying glass uses a
questions.explanation: A magnifying glass is a convex lens.

questions.question: To use a convex lens as a magnifying glass, the object must be placed
questions.explanation: The object must be within the focal length to produce a virtual, magnified image.

questions.question: The image formed by a magnifying glass is
questions.explanation: The image is virtual, erect, and magnified.

questions.question: A rectangular glass prism can be used to deviate a ray of light through
questions.explanation: A rectangular prism can deviate light through 90° by total internal reflection.

questions.question: The type of mirror used in a car headlamp to produce a parallel beam is a
options: Concave mirror with the bulb at its focus
Parabolic mirror with the bulb at its focus
questions.explanation: A parabolic mirror with the bulb at its focus produces a parallel beam.

questions.question: Which of the following is used in a simple slide projector to ensure that the slide is uniformly illuminated?
questions.explanation: A condenser lens spreads light uniformly over the slide.

questions.question: Which of the following optical instruments produces a virtual, erect and magnified image of a nearby object?
questions.explanation: A simple microscope (magnifying glass) produces a virtual, erect, magnified image.

questions.question: The combination of a convex objective of long focal length and a convex eyepiece of short focal length is used in the construction of a
questions.explanation: An astronomical telescope uses a long-focus objective and a short-focus eyepiece.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT an application of total internal reflection?
questions.explanation: A magnifying glass uses refraction, not total internal reflection.
